observations: Photo 0 shows the front of an LG monitor displaying a game interface (FC26) with the LG logo at the bottom center of the bezel.
Photo 1 shows the left side of the monitor, with the LG logo visible on the lower left bezel and the screen displaying the same game interface.

Photo 2 shows the back of the monitor, with the LG logo on the lower left, a textured black plastic back panel, and ports including HDMI, DisplayPort, and audio out. The stand is attached and appears to be fixed, not adjustable.
The monitor is placed on a red surface, likely a desk or cabinet, with shelves and computer towers in the background.
The screen appears to be working and displaying color accurately in the photos.
No visible cracks, dead pixels, or physical damage to the screen or casing is evident in the photos.
The model number '27MP65HQ' is not visible in any photo, though the seller claims it.

claims.claim: A clean and fully functional LG 27MP65HQ 27-inch monitor.
claims.evidence: The LG brand is visible in all photos, but the model number '27MP65HQ' is not visible in any photo. The 'fully functional' claim cannot be verified remotely; screen performance, ports, and internal components are not testable from photos.

claims.claim: It features an IPS panel with Full HD.
claims.evidence: The screen appears to display color well, but panel type (IPS) and resolution (Full HD) cannot be confirmed from photos alone. These are technical specifications not visible in the images.

risks.risk: The monitor may not be the claimed model 27MP65HQ, or may be a different model with different specifications.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the model label on the back or bottom of the monitor, or a screenshot from the monitor's on-screen display (OSD) showing the model number.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic 27-inch LG monitor, which may be less valuable than the 27MP65HQ.

risks.risk: The monitor may have dead pixels, screen burn-in, or backlight issues not visible in the current display.
risks.proof: A photo of the screen displaying a solid white, black, and red/green/blue screen to check for dead or stuck pixels.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as potentially defective, with a discount for unverified screen quality.

risks.risk: The monitor may not be fully functional — ports may be damaged or non-working, or it may not power on or display properly under different inputs.
risks.proof: A video showing the monitor powering on, switching between inputs (HDMI, DisplayPort), and displaying content from different sources.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not working, since remote functionality cannot be confirmed.

proof_requests: A clear photo of the model label on the back or bottom of the monitor.
A video showing the monitor powering on, switching inputs, and displaying content from different sources.
Photos of the screen displaying solid white, black, and primary colors to check for dead pixels.
response.reason: The model number is not visible in any photo, and the 'fully functional' claim cannot be verified remotely. Without proof of the exact model and working condition, the item cannot be priced accurately. The risks of misrepresentation or hidden defects are significant.
